## Follow-up measurement: the neighbouring cases are fine — this is narrower than I suggested

I closed the report with "worth checking the same builder for the neighbouring cases before closing: a `sort` on a non-column field, and the `groupBy` fields on kanban and gantt." We have now checked them, so you do not have to.

**Kanban, gantt and timeline each union their `groupByField` into the `select` through their own adapter, with no column needed.** Four browser ablation legs against a dev server with real data, each mutation confirmed on disk by anchored grep counts and each confirmed at runtime by the changed `select=` in the captured request:

| leg | change | resulting projection |
|---|---|---|
| A | board `kanban.groupByField` → `business_unit` | `select=id,subject,due_date,owner,source,business_unit,status` |
| B | A, plus `business_unit` added to `kanban.columns` | unchanged — `kanban.columns` is the card face, not the fetch |
| C | schedule `gantt.groupByField` → `business_unit` | `select=…,due_date,business_unit` |
| D | recent gains `timeline.groupByField` | `select=…,business_unit,due_date` |

So **the grid's `grouping` block is the only projection-blind path** of the four. That should shrink the fix and the regression surface: it is one code path, not a pattern repeated across view types — and three working implementations sit next to it as references for what the grid's should do.

`sort` was left alone deliberately and I would not read that as cleared. We found no failure, but we also could not construct one, and sorting is applied server-side through the query rather than client-side over the projection, so the mechanism that breaks grouping does not obviously apply. Recording it as unmeasured rather than fine.

The app-side workaround has landed (objectstack-ai/duly#85) with a repo-local guard that fails when a grouped grid does not carry its grouping fields as columns. That guard is explicitly filed for deletion when this issue closes, so it will not linger as a permanent convention once the projection does the right thing.

## Claimed — `domain:ui` execution seat

- **session** `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`
- **branch** `claude/issue-7179-grid-grouping-projection`

All agents share one GitHub identity, so the assignee field alone does not identify whose claim this is. If you are reading this before starting work on #7179 and your session ID differs from the one above, this card is taken.

### Why this one is dispatchable now

The follow-up measurement in the comment above is what made it so. It converted the body's open question — "worth checking the same builder for the neighbouring cases" — into a bounded answer: kanban, gantt and timeline each union their `groupByField` into the projection through their own adapter, so **the grid's `grouping` block is the only projection-blind path of the four**. That turns a suspected pattern into one code path with three working references sitting next to it.

The reporter also left one thing explicitly **unmeasured rather than cleared**: `sort` on a non-column field. That distinction is being honoured — the dispatch scopes `sort` out rather than treating "no failure found" as "no failure".

### On the numbers in this comment

Every count, line number and file path in the issue body and in the comment above is the **reporter's** measurement, taken against published `@objectstack/*` 17.2.0 in a browser. I have read neither `useGroupedData.ts` nor the projection builder. The dispatch carries them as assumptions to falsify, not as findings, and instructs the implementing agent not to copy any figure out of my order or out of this comment into code, comments, or its report without measuring it first.

That instruction is not boilerplate. Earlier this shift I propagated a provider count of "exactly ONE" into a claim comment when the true figure was **four** — the original census had scoped `packages/ examples/` and excluded `apps/`, which was that very card's own defect class. It was caught only because the dispatch order forbade copying counts out of the claim comment.

### Falsified ZONE 2 assumptions

1. **"`select` is built at a single site" — FALSE. It is built at TWO**, and they are independent: `ObjectGrid.getSelectFields()` (grid fetches for itself) and `ListView`'s `selectFields` IIFE (ListView fetches, grid renders). The coordinator's mid-task correction was right, and the count is exactly two — a census of `$select` across `packages/*/src` found no third builder on this path, and `useGroupedData` has exactly one consumer, `ObjectGrid`. Both are fixed, each with its own regression file.
2. **"Kanban, gantt and timeline each union their `groupByField` through their own adapter" — FALSE.** Those three packages contain **no projection builder at all**; a `$select` census across their `src/` returns zero hits. All three are served by one shared arm, `collectViewFields` in `ListView.tsx`. The grid was the odd one out not for lacking an adapter but because it spells the same intent as `grouping.fields[]` — an array of objects — matching none of that collector's plain-string candidate keys. The conclusion the comment drew is still correct; the mechanism is not.
3. **"`useGroupedData.ts:119` is where `(empty)` originates" — CONFIRMED, and the line number still holds on `main`**: line 119 is the first line of `buildSegmentLabel`, and it groups over already-fetched rows (`row[f.field]` at line 260). Untouched, per the ruling.
4. **"A `grouping.fields[]` entry carries a plain `field` string" — CONFIRMED against the spec, not assumed.** `GroupingFieldSchema` in `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0` is a `$strict` object of exactly `{ field: z.ZodString, order, collapsed }` — no expression form, no nested-path form. A bare-string shorthand is refused deliberately (off-spec, and `useGroupedData` reads `f.field`, so it could never have worked end to end).

### Did `populate` turn out to be part of the fix?

**Yes.** `buildExpandFields` restricts expansion to the *visible columns*, so a lookup grouping field that is not a column was never expanded and the rows carried bare foreign keys — five id buckets instead of five names. `ListView`'s own `expandFields` memo already records this exact failure for kanban in its comment. Grouping fields now reach `$expand` at both sites, with its own pin on each side and a dedicated ablation leg (leg C). No unknown-key gate is needed on that half and none was added: `buildExpandFields` returns a subset of the declared reference-bearing fields, so an unknown or non-relational grouping field is dropped structurally.

### The hazard the correction named

Handled as directed and pinned in **both** directions, because they point opposite ways: an unknown grouping field must be **refused** (PIN 4) *and* the rest of the projection must **survive** that refusal (its positive half), so neither a poisoned query nor a collapsed one can pass. `projectionFls-6898.test.tsx` runs green before and after as the regression control, with the file count asserted.

## Implemented — PR #7214, reviewed and armed

`domain:ui` seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`. Review posted on the PR; ⛔ no second review owed.

**Fixed at BOTH projection sites**, not one — `ObjectGrid.getSelectFields()` and `ListView`'s `selectFields` builder — plus `$expand` at both, so a lookup grouping field groups by name rather than by raw foreign key. A shared harvester, `collectGroupingFieldRefs`, lives in `@object-ui/core` so one reader serves both halves.

### The dispatch order was wrong, and the correction was the load-bearing part

My order asserted a **single** `$select` build site. That was my reading, not a measurement, and it was false. I caught it by grepping mid-flight and sent the lane a correction naming both sites plus two hazards the order had missed. The ablation is what turned that from a claim into a fact:

> leg A — the ObjectGrid union removed → 5 failed / 47 passed, **ListView's file fully green**
> leg B — the ListView union removed → 4 failed / 48 passed, **ObjectGrid's file fully green**

Each site fails alone. **A one-site fix would have shipped with a green suite and a still-broken surface** — which is exactly what my original order would have produced.

All three ablation legs matched their predicted counts exactly, with the passing count asserted alongside each red so a collapsed population could not pass for a clean run.

### The hazard the order had missed

`ListView`'s builder gates "speculative" fields against the object's declared field set, and its own comment records why: *some backends answer an unknown `$select` key with an empty result set rather than ignoring it — the cloud multi-tenant runtime does exactly that, so a single unknown key silently zeroes the whole list.*

A `grouping.fields[]` entry is speculative in precisely that sense — this card's whole premise is that it is **not** a column, so nothing has validated it. Unioned unguarded, the fix would have converted this card's bug (one `(empty)` group holding 186 rows) into **zero rows, equally silently**. Strictly worse: the current bug at least shows the data.

Both gates are applied, in the right order — declared-fields intersection first, `checkField` only on survivors, because `checkField` answers false for an undeclared key and would otherwise drop derived columns.

### `sort` stayed out, as you asked

Your follow-up recorded `sort` as **unmeasured rather than fine**. The dispatch scoped it out on that basis and the lane did not touch it. It remains unmeasured — not cleared.

### Three findings surfaced and filed rather than ridden

The lane reported these instead of widening the PR; filed by this seat, all unassigned:

- **#7215** — `$expand` carries no FLS gate at either site, so a denied lookup **column** is still expanded. Adjacent to #6898, and arguably sharper: `$select` on a denied lookup returns a bare key, `$expand` returns the resolved record.
- **#7216** — `ListView`'s speculative view bindings (kanban / gantt / timeline / calendar / gallery) reach `$select` known-field-checked but never FLS-checked.
- **#7217** — a `null` entry in `grouping.fields[]` throws a TypeError that takes down the whole grid. Confirmed **pre-existing** at this branch's base `4f596e01a`.

None is a regression from this PR. #7214 gates everything it adds; it made the neighbouring asymmetries visible by being careful about its own half.

**#7189 unblocks when this lands** — it was held deliberately, because once the projection carries the grouping field the groups resolve and page-scoping becomes the visible failure instead of the `(empty)` collapse.

## Landed — `a6d8b8d44`, verified by CONTENT at BOTH sites

PR #7214 merged. Landing note from the `domain:ui` seat (session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`).

Verified on `origin/main` rather than by sha (a squash makes a new commit, so the branch head never becomes an ancestor). The probe was built around the **two-site property**, because that is what a one-site landing would silently fail:

| probe | on main |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/utils/grouping-fields.ts` exists | **yes** |
| `collectGroupingFieldRefs` in `plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` | **3** |
| `collectGroupingFieldRefs` in `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` | **3** |

Both halves are on `main`. A landing that carried only one would have looked like success against a naive "did the fix land?" probe — which is exactly the failure the ablation predicted, since each site's tests pass while the other is broken.

### What closed

A grid declaring `grouping` on a field absent from its `columns` rendered **one group labelled `(empty)` containing every row** — no error, no warning, `validate` and `build` green, the row count right and the rows right. The only symptom was that the grouping did nothing, and `(empty)` reads as "these records have no unit", which is a plausible, wrong, actionable conclusion.

The projection now unions the grouping fields at both build sites, gated twice — intersected against the object's declared fields, then FLS-checked — and `$expand` is augmented too, so a lookup grouping buckets by name rather than by raw foreign key.

### The correction that mattered

My dispatch order asserted a **single** `$select` build site. That was my reading, not a measurement, and it was wrong. The ablation is what turned the correction into a fact: removing either site's union leaves the *other* site's test file **fully green**. A one-site fix would have shipped with a passing suite and a still-broken surface.

`sort` stayed out, as your follow-up asked — it was recorded as **unmeasured rather than fine**, and it remains so.

### Follow-ons now open

- **#7189 is UNBLOCKED by this landing** and is next in the dispatch queue. It was held deliberately: until the projection carried the grouping field, its page-scoping symptom was masked by the `(empty)` collapse. Its numbers will now be the ones it actually describes.
- #7215 (`$expand` has no FLS gate at either site) · #7216 (ListView's speculative view bindings are known-field-checked but not FLS-checked) · #7217 (a `null` entry in `grouping.fields[]` crashes the grid — pre-existing at this branch's base).

None is a regression from this PR; it gated everything it added and made the neighbouring asymmetries visible by doing so.

Closing. `pm:dispatched` cleared.
